resources.string: Your notes are saved as plain Markdown files in one folder on this tablet. Share that folder with your computer, and Obsidian or any AI tool that reads files can use your notes. No account and no cloud needed.
Nothing exported yet. Open a note and tap Save & Exit.
Set it in General under Vault inbox folder. Use a folder inside your Obsidian vault on the tablet, or keep the default.
Syncthing copies a folder between your devices, directly and privately. Install Syncthing-Fork from F-Droid (or Syncthing from Google Play), open it and allow storage access.
Share the folder from the tablet
In Syncthing tap Folders, then +, choose the notes folder above, and under Sharing add your computer using its device ID (in Syncthing on the computer: Actions, Show ID).
Install Syncthing on your computer, accept the tablet and the folder, and choose where it lands: a folder inside your Obsidian vault, or any folder you like. New notes arrive within seconds.
Let your AI read your notes

Every note is a .md file with a title, date and #tags, plus its page images. Point your AI tool or agent at that folder on your computer and it can search and read your notes as text. Obsidian shows them as normal notes.
Only devices you approve in Syncthing receive your notes.
Optional: sync notes to your computer
Share your notes as Markdown with Obsidian or your AI tools using Syncthing. It takes about five minutes, and you can do it later in Settings, Sync.
